text: The LORD said to Moses, "See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.
You are to speak everything I command you, and your brother Aaron is to tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites go out of his land.
But I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and though I multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt,
Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will lay my hand on Egypt, and with mighty acts of judgment I will bring my divisions, my people the Israelites, out of the land of Egypt.
And the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I stretch out my hand against Egypt and bring the Israelites out from among them."
Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded them.
Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"When Pharaoh says to you, 'Perform a wonder,' say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh, and it will become a serpent.'"

versions.text: "When Pharaoh says to you, 'Perform a wonder,' then say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh,' and it will become a serpent."
versions.explanation: In the Hebrew, "let it become a serpent" belongs to the words Moses is to speak to Aaron; the current punctuation places it outside the inner quotation, making it a narrator's aside. Keeping it inside the quotation is more accurate and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just as the LORD had commanded. Aaron threw his staff down before Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a serpent.
Then Pharaoh summoned the wise men and sorcerers, and the Egyptian magicians did the same thing by their secret arts.
Each one threw down his staff, and they became serpents. But Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs.
Yet Pharaoh's heart grew hard, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Pharaoh's heart is unyielding; he refuses to let the people go.
Go to Pharaoh in the morning as he is going out to the water. Stand and wait for him on the bank of the Nile, and take in your hand the staff that turned into a snake.
Say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to tell you: Let my people go, so that they may worship me in the wilderness. But until now you have not listened.
This is what the LORD says: By this you will know that I am the LORD. Watch: with the staff in my hand I will strike the water of the Nile, and it will turn to blood.
The fish in the Nile will die, the river will stink, and the Egyptians will not be able to bear drinking water from the Nile.'"

versions.text: The fish in the Nile will die, the river will stink, and the Egyptians will not be able to drink its water.'"
versions.explanation: The verb נִלְאוּ means "grow weary of / loathe / find it impossible," which is distinct from the plain "could not" (יָכְלוּ) used in verse 21. Preserving the difference keeps the prediction and its fulfilment from sounding identical.

text: The LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt—over their rivers and canals, their ponds and all their reservoirs—and they will turn to blood.' There will be blood everywhere in Egypt, even in vessels of wood and stone."
Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded. In the sight of Pharaoh and his officials, Aaron raised the staff and struck the water of the Nile, and all the water in the river turned to blood.
The fish in the Nile died, the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink its water. There was blood throughout the land of Egypt.
But the Egyptian magicians did the same thing by their secret arts, and Pharaoh's heart grew hard. He would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he paid no attention to this either.
And all the Egyptians dug along the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink the water of the river.
Seven days passed after the LORD struck the Nile.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me.
If you refuse to let them go, I am about to plague your whole territory with frogs.

versions.text: If you refuse to let them go, I will plague your whole territory with frogs.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי with the participle expresses imminent action ("look, I am about to..."), which the flat future "I will" loses. The revision keeps the urgency of the threat without adding words that break the rhythm.

text: The Nile will teem with frogs. They will come up and go into your palace, into your bedroom and onto your bed, into the houses of your officials and your people, into your ovens and your kneading troughs.
The frogs will swarm over you and your people and all your officials.'"
